module_title: CKA Week 1 - Foundations and kubectl Speed
title: CKA Week 1 Speed Drill - 34 kubectl Tasks
description: A 34-task speed drill over the Week 1 CKA domains: namespaces, pods, deployments, rollouts, services, config objects and fast exports. The exam shell (k, kn, $do, $now) is already configured - every task is real cluster work.
scenario: It is the Wednesday lab day of Week 1: 34 tasks, exam conditions. Everything you create here is something the CKA exam asks you to produce in under 60 seconds. No copy-paste from the browser: type every command.
symptoms: The clock is the opponent: each task should cost under 60 seconds after warm-up
Checks verify live cluster state, so how you build each object does not matter
mission: Complete all 40 tasks: set up the exam shell, create namespaces, pods, deployments, services, config objects and export YAML - at speed, from memory, with the docs closed.

hints.title: Do the shell setup first
hints.content: Tasks 1-6 are pure exam muscle memory: alias k, $do, $now, kn, completion, vim settings. Every later task gets faster once these exist. Persist them with >> so the checks find them in ~/.bashrc.

hints.title: Imperative first, YAML only when forced
hints.content: create deploy/expose/scale/set image cover most tasks. Only env vars, labels beyond -l, resources and multi-container pods need $do + edit + apply.

hints.title: Rollouts are annotations
hints.content: kubectl rollout history/undo is tracked in the deployment.kubernetes.io/revision annotation. set image bumps it, undo bumps it again - task 21 checks revision >= 2, task 22 wants >= 3.

hints.title: Seeded pod
hints.content: A pod named doomed is pre-created in the default namespace. Task 33 just wants it gone - use your $now alias for practice.

hints.title: Export with $do
hints.content: kubectl run x --image=... $do > file.yaml is the exam way to produce YAML. sed or vim the file when the task asks for a different image or field.
